The verifier checked the wording against the 1874 second edition while the source line names the first publication, William Blackwood and Sons 1871 to 1872, so the card could have been printing 1874 wording under an 1871 to 1872 byline. I went to the first edition itself: Internet Archive item india.history.resource.84460, Middlemarch, Book VIII, Sunset and Sunrise, the last page before THE END, imprint PRINTED BY WILLIAM BLACKWOOD AND SONS, EDINBURGH. The closing sentence there is word for word the quotation, including the colon after diffusive, the semicolon after unhistoric acts, and the comma after have been. The 1874 revision of the Finale touched the earlier paragraph about modes of education and propositions of marriage from a sickly man, which the 1872 scan still carries and which the 1874 text drops; it did not touch this sentence. Wikisource's 1874 Finale gives the identical sentence, so both editions agree and the source line is honest either way. Other checks: it is the last sentence of the Finale and so of the novel, which is what the source claims; the narrator speaks, so no speaker is owed; shipped.js returns no shipped line and no near match, and records George Eliot under mary ann evans at two for the year in months 1 and 2, so this is her permitted third and no other September candidate is hers; the tag Fiction is the form of the work; the source line leads with the name, carries no dash and runs 102 characters; nothing in the misattribution list touches it; it is pre-2000, not scripture, film, lyric, proverb, business or oratory, and needs no content warning. Nothing to refute.
